claims.claim_text: Elizabeth Cecilia Briefs, later Elizabeth Cecilia Clancy, is the best-supported identity for the indexed Elizabeth C. Briefs and is documented as a wartime OSS translator.
claims.evidence_excerpt: During World War II Elizabeth worked as a translator for the OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The obituary identifies Elizabeth Cecilia Clancy by her Briefs family name and describes her wartime OSS translation work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare exact birth surname, matching middle initial expanded to Cecilia, and direct OSS context. No service identifier or digitized personnel-file link was available for confirmation.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source places the translator role during World War II but does not identify a pre-OSS employer or show when OSS work began.
claims.match_notes: The married surname is preserved as a documented variant. Her father's university employment is not attributed to her.

sources.locator_override: Biographical paragraph describing World War II work
sources.excerpt_override: During World War II Elizabeth worked as a translator for the OSS.

claims.claim_text: William Biggar Brierly is the best-supported identity for the indexed William B. Brierly; a professional memorial documents that he began OSS work in 1942.
claims.evidence_excerpt: In 1942 he began working for the Office of Strategic Services.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The memorial gives Brierly's full middle name, education chronology, and the year he entered OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact surname and initial, the expanded middle name Biggar, and direct OSS chronology. The available sources do not expose a service identifier for official-file confirmation.
claims.temporal_assessment: The memorial places his OSS entry in 1942, the same year Clark records his geography doctorate.
claims.match_notes: The full middle name is added only as a sourced variant; the printed index spelling remains unchanged.

sources.excerpt_override: In 1942 he began working for the Office of Strategic Services.

claims.claim_text: Clark University doctoral student is the best-supported immediate pre-OSS status for William Brierly: Clark records his Ph.D. in 1942, and a memorial dates his OSS entry to 1942.
claims.evidence_excerpt: In 1942 he began working for the Office of Strategic Services.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Clark's institutional index records Brierly's 1942 geography doctorate, while the memorial says his OSS work began in 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The unusual name and matching 1942 education chronology connect the institutional and professional sources to the indexed person at high confidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: The same-year sequence is strongly date-bounded but not an explicit statement that he left Clark directly for OSS. Student status is not classified as employment.
claims.match_notes: No named civilian employer has been established. The Clark relationship is excluded from employer analytics and remains separately labeled as student status.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lawrence J. Brigante is confirmed as Army Captain Lawrence Joseph Brigante by a contemporary OSS board report and its exact private-identifier match.
claims.evidence_excerpt: LAWRENCE JOSEPH BRIGANTE, Captain, Corps of Military Police
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official report supplies Brigante's full name, Army rank and branch, OSS entry chronology, and the same private identifier printed in the index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact full name, matching middle initial, matching rank and branch context, direct OSS service, and an exact private-identifier match. The identifier is withheld publicly.
claims.temporal_assessment: The report was created in May 1944 and retrospectively states his August 1943 OSS entry and prior Army office.
claims.match_notes: The public profile masks the private identifier and publishes only the evidence needed for identity and chronology.
